courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So this is how we deploy our apps to the app stores which of course is one of the main reasons why you
often use Ionic and Capacitor but you are not limited to that. All the time,
we were testing a web app in the browser, so why don't we deploy it as such
and actually, we already got one.
Since we ran ng build prod earlier in this module, we have this www folder which holds a web app that
can be used just like that, that is ready to be deployed to a web server and actually let me show this
to you by using Firebase.
However, I don't just want to publish a regular web app,
I want to publish a progressive web app. Now,
what turns a web into a progressive web app?
It still is a web app,
it just uses a service worker which can cache certain assets on the front-end to serve your app faster
on subsequent requests and in general, make your app feel a bit more native-like whilst running in the
browser.
You can take my complete progressive web app course if you want to learn all about that exciting technology.
Turning an Angular app in a progressive web app is straightforward,
you just run ng add @angular/pwa for progressive web app and this will now configure this
Angular project such that it automatically generates such a service worker that is responsible for that
caching and so on and basically sets up everything you need to have a progressive web app,
nothing else needed. Once all of that is done,
you'll have an ngsw-config.json file which allows you to configure that service worker. Now more information
about that can be found on the official Angular docs under techniques,
service workers and PWA, there you'll learn more about what you can configure there and how it works.
This generally sets up which of your assets will be cached in which way and that caching again will
happen in the browser once users have visited your page to make subsequent visits faster and potentially
even provide offline support.
Now with all of that added, you don't need to change anything,
the defaults are pretty good and you can run ng build --prod again to now build the Angular
app again taking this new configuration into account.
Side note, of course you can also set a fav icon for example here by adding icons into your assets folder,
you get the Angular icon
out of the box, you can replace that fav icon which is the Ionic icon and these Android icons here
with your own icons that should have the sizes that are encoded here in the file names
if you want to have your own icons for your web app as well. I will not do it here
since it's not really a difficult task, it's just a time consuming one,
instead let's wait for this build to finish and let me then show you how you could deploy this to Firebase,
though of course you can deploy it to any static host like AWS S3 or whatever your favorite static
website host is. The static host thing is important though since it's a front-end driven web app with
HTML, front-end, Javascript and CSS only, you need no PHP or NodeJS server on the back-end, you really
need only a host that is capable of serving HTML, Javascript and CSS, like Firebase hosting or
AWS S3.
So building the project finished,
now I want to as I mentioned before deploy this to Firebase but just as an example,
you're not limited to Firebase. Since you already added Firebase cloud functions though, adding hosting
is particularly easy,
you simply run Firebase init again in your project and we already added functions in the past,
now we also add hosting here.
So simply check hosting and hit tap,
now what do you want as your public directory?
Here we'll use www because that is the folder that holds our build assets. We want to configure this
as a single page app,
yes because that's what it is,
so enter a y here.
I don't want to overwrite my index.html file, instead I want to use the one I had and with that,
we got this firebase.json file with some configuration about the the hosting which you should leave
as it is, the default should work here.
We can now run Firebase deploy here and this will now deploy our cloud function as it did before but it will
also now deploy our web app to Firebase hosting.
So let's wait for that to finish and once this is done, you see the URL where your app will be hosted
at here,
of course you can also connect your own domains here if you want to stick to Firebase hosting, the official
docs tell you more. If I enter that domain here into the browser though, I see my web app here and obviously
feel free to adjust this styling to whatever you want but this is now our web app
as we built it throughout this course and as it also runs as a native app but now here in the browser
and it works just as it does on the mobile devices, this is the app we built where we can book our events and
so on.
So that is our web app we built
and you also learned how to deploy this app as a native app.
Therefore I hope you now have all the tools you need to build amazing apps, use amazing features and
then of course deploy them to any platform you want to deploy them to.
